RECOIL interleaves attribute rows by field (lines 0/2 and 1/3) in this 152-line, non-interlaced picture, giving colour fringes on the top/bottom edge of every shape (white bar on the arrow head, cyan specks on the tomato). The interleave is for interlaced (400-line) pictures only; with one attribute row per 4-line cell every clip-art shape is clean. Output reviewed.

RECOIL rejects 10018-byte Saracen Paint files (load $7800, ending at $9F1F before colour RAM rows 20-24). This file is a byte-exact prefix of RECOIL's own test.sar (10219 bytes), whose missing 201-byte tail is all zeros; zero-filling gives a render identical to RECOIL's test.sar. Output reviewed: 'Life on the Loadstar' boy fishing.

RECOIL rejects 10018-byte Saracen Paint files (load $7800, ending at $9F1F; same short variant as 1.sar, a prefix of test.sar). No bitmap pixel in rows 20-24 uses colour RAM, so the missing tail does not affect the picture. Screen $7800 / bitmap $7C00 / colour $9C00 verified: colour at $9C00 renders cleanly, other offsets do not. Output reviewed: 'Army' logo with smiley.

RECOIL rejects packed Funpaint II with trailing bytes. The ESC count value RLE (CB Funpaint 2) unpacks to the full 33676-byte image and ends with the usual 'ESC 00' end marker like every other packed sample, then 65 $1A bytes pad the file to 241x128 bytes (XMODEM/CP-M SUB padding). Output reviewed: IFLI portrait of a smiling man.

RECOIL rejects packed Funpaint II with trailing bytes. RLE unpacks to the full 33676-byte image ending with the usual 'ESC 00' end marker, then 98 $1A bytes pad the file to 98x128 bytes (XMODEM/CP-M SUB padding). Output reviewed: IFLI Peoria skyline with riverboats, 'HM' signature.

One pixel differs, at (45,109) in a reversed @ (screen code $80). The C64 character ROM 901225-01 (MD5 12a4202f5331d45af846af6c58fba946) stores row 5 of the reversed @ as $99, not $9D (the inverse of @ row 5, $62), and the VIC-II displays ROM bytes as they are; RECOIL draws the exact inverse. All other 255 glyphs of both sets are exact inverses, so this is the only pixel. Output reviewed: same picture as RECOIL apart from that pixel.

RECOIL paints both sprite layers of packed Super Hires FLI in the first colour (unpacked $1FE8); the lower layer uses the second ($1FE9), as unpacked SHF does ($43E8/$43E9). Checked in Crest's Super Hires FLI Editor V1.0 (SHF_V1_Fix.prg from c64.rulez.org) run in VICE: after loading this file with colours patched to 2/5, $D027-$D02A = 2 and $D02B-$D02E = 5, and the editor's screen matches our decode with 0 of 16032 pixels inconsistent (2907 with RECOIL's single colour). Output reviewed: zebra with grey shading layer.

FLI Designer picture (17218 bytes) followed by 62 bytes of 0x1A, the CP/M record padding (17280 = 135 x 128). RECOIL does not recognise the padded size and falls through to another layout, giving a mostly black picture with green and grey streaks. Our decode of the first 17218 bytes is a clean rider on a horse with the title King's Daughter at the top. Output reviewed.

RECOIL reads this 10018-byte file (load $2000) in Koala order and renders a sheared picture. It is Advanced Art Studio (bitmap $2000, screen $3F40, colour $4338): recoil2png on a copy renamed .ocp shows a clean multicolour spaceship with a PARALLAX / Ocean logo, and our output is pixel-identical to that render. Output reviewed.
